I am getting old — 71 years now — and my back is not what it was. My son works in the city, so I mostly manage the land myself with my wife helping in busy seasons. I have about 6 mu of flat land. I have grown wheat and corn on this land for 40 years. I know this land. I am not going to try anything new.

The government agent came by last year and said we should use less water, but the well is still there and the crops need water. I will irrigate as I always have. My neighbor switched to a new hybrid corn seed last year and got a good harvest. I will ask him for the seed dealer's name and buy that too.

For one small plot — maybe 1 mu near the house — my wife grows vegetables: garlic, cabbage, and some sweet potato. We eat from that. I do not count it in the main plan because we do not sell it.

For fertilizer, I use the compound bag fertilizer from the township supply station. I apply it before planting and top-dress once. I do not have a soil test — never have. I apply roughly what my father applied, maybe a little more because the soil is older now and tired.

I will plough the wheat field in autumn with the village's small rotary tiller (I pay the operator by the mu). For corn, I just direct seed into the stubble — saves money and my body cannot handle too much heavy work anymore.
